The lcm of generic residue orders equals the Brauer period because the unramified class on Y vanishes. Secondary node order divides both generic orders. The actual Azumaya root-extension construction works componentwise at the generic DVRs and extends in codimension two on the regular mixed-root stack; its Kummer lift is corrected by a line from Y.

The local Kummer symbol gives the commutator and preserves scalar power data. The mixed-order scalar algebra has centre generated by X^h and Y^h, splits as (bc/h^2) copies of M_h, and ordinary root characters act transitively on these blocks.

The generic character torsor is connected of degree m_i. At a node, the neighboring inertia acts by an h_x-cycle; consequently the coarse cover has ramification h_x, m_i/h_x points and remaining root stabilizer m_j/h_x. Riemann-Hurwitz and rank r=m_i*s_i have the stated exact factors.

The spectral root curve has vanishing prime-to-p Brauer class by the cyclic-root Leray calculation, so the neutralizing-line Morita description is valid. Formal lifts occur over the adjacent-root-marked stack, not a falsely unramified coarse cover.

All-ring node gluing uses actual projective multiplicity modules for the split finite algebra, framed locally, plus Milnor pasting and exact invariants. Scalar cancellation makes Hom factor through the abelian root quotient even though bundle inertia is noncommutative; each character has exactly the asserted number of monomials in the rectangle.

The algebraic Azumaya twisted bundle tensored with all root characters contains every inertia irreducible and yields a genuine generating bundle. Its possibly large rank is explicitly excluded from coordinate estimates. No general-graph count is asserted.
